rules_evaluated.evidence: L109 (closest to flattening the mood): "Two signatures, earned. Your staff engineer sees a test-strategy skill tuned to this codebase, your CISO sees a STRIDE decision with an ADR." This is the strategy doc's M3 mood verbatim in module voice — doc L245 pins M3 at 'Earned trust — "the way I work with agents is something my staff engineer and my CISO can sign off on, before I even try anything big"', and the file's Meta block L142 restates that sentence exactly as its mood target. The state the student leaves in: covered by two named stakeholders, and explicitly not yet stretched ('before I even try anything big'). It sets up M4's curious readiness rather than resolving it — L109's second half hands the discipline forward ('Module 4 turns the discipline inward') and L95 makes the M4 task the student's own open call. Nothing here closes the arc early.

M3's mood is earned trust, not unease, so the punitive/epistemic split has only one candidate passage. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked all six Key Concepts bullets (L76–81) asking which of the doc's six themes each instances. L78 "A test-strategy skill authored on your codebase is worth more than a perfect generic one. Your codebase teaches the skill, not the manual." = theme 5 (the agent is trying to capture your world). L79 "Ask the agent what's weakest about its own output; it surfaces what your read skips. Same-window self-audits under-flag, so push past the first answer." = theme 4 (mechanically self-aware, grain of salt) — the caveat clause is the grain of salt, in module language. L80 "The team kit grows by accretion" = theme 2 (the system is built by compounding). L76 "The labor is delegated; the judgment isn't" = theme 3 (the LLM is a mirror; the operator is the ceiling). Four theme-instances against a 2–3 floor, each phrased in the module's own vocabulary rather than the doc's. Closest to a bare tactic with no theme behind it: L77 "The access surface is what STRIDE chews on. STRIDE before access-mapping is threat-modeling pub-quiz" — this one is sequencing craft rather than a theme instance, which is fine while four others carry the load.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — theme breadcrumbs, not standalone section.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Gates first. §5: cleared above. §3: no bullet leads on a failure word (grep → 0). §4: no bullet reaches into M4–M6 territory. Survivors then read for breadcrumbs, not scanned for a marker. Three bullets land on a compact closing clause: L76 "Invoke, don't re-derive." (5 words, names the move), L78 "Your codebase teaches the skill, not the manual." (8 words), L80 "an untested skill in the team kit is slop-sharing" (9 words). Three is the ceiling, not over it. grep -c 'Remember:' on the body → 0, and no bolded breadcrumb wrapper survives — the retired labelled form is absent. Variety check against adjacent modules, per the never-ship-the-same-breadcrumb-verbatim clause: `plan-mode-done-right.md` (M2) closes bullets on "Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part." and "The skill is old; only the surface is new."; `run-the-first-experiment.md` (M4) carries no breadcrumb clause at all. No verbatim or near-verbatim overlap with M3's three, and no theme fires as a breadcrumb in both M2 and M3. Directional discipline holds: L76's breadcrumb names the move (invoke) rather than a trust ratio.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: What You'll Learn shape — capability register, not syllabus.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Gates first: §3 clear (no failure-word leads), §4 clear (no bullet teaches an M4+ moment). Apparatus check is mechanical and clean — grep -Ec '\((Analyze|Evaluate|Create|Understand|Apply|Remember)\)' on the body → 0 (pattern proven: same grep returns 3 on a planted '(Analyze)' string); Bloom lives at L138 in the Meta block where §7(i) puts it. No author-defence aside (no 'not a…' carve-out anywhere in L22–27), no didactic taxonomy stamp. Register check: strip each bullet to verb + immediate object and every one reads as work a peer would recognise — Fork a worktree / Invoke curated skills / Split jobs / Author a skill / Test the skill / Ship one skill. Closest to a mechanism tail is L23 "**Invoke** curated access-control-analysis and STRIDE skills on a feature you're shipping (each as a subagent, fresh context): name what your first read missed, pick one threat worth hardening against, and write the decision as an ADR in your repo's convention" — the tail is not a pedagogical mechanism ('by mapping each piece to…') but three further actions the student performs, and the parenthetical is the §7(c) brief-operational carve-out. L27's "and know when it's a team PR" is outcome-side, carve-out (a). Grammar-fit holds throughout: the concrete-artifact bullets take verbs of construction (Fork, Author, Build-shaped Ship), and 'Earn' is correctly NOT forced onto them.

todos.rule: check_strategy_tie_in.md §7 — 'Strategic theme verbs LEAD bullets — sister of §5'
todos.note: None of the six What You'll Learn bullets (L22–27) leads with an AE101 theme verb (Compound / Earn / Mirror / Ground / Introspect / Sharpen / Capture), in the module whose own title is 'Earn the trust' and whose close section is 'Sharpen the skill from evidence'. Not blocking: §7's grammar-fit clause explicitly refuses 'Earn' on concrete artifact lists, and every verb present (Fork, Invoke, Split, Author, Test, Ship) is engineer-register and passes the strip-to-verb-plus-object test. The observation is only that a whole module's signposting carries zero theme verbs while §7 says the themes recur through them across the training. The one bullet where a theme verb would fit without strain is L25 '**Author** a test-strategy skill through conversation…' → '**Capture** your codebase's testing conventions into a skill, through conversation with Claude (one question at a time)' — theme 5, and the object is abstract enough for the verb. Maintainer call, not a defect.
